_note: Playstyle for the Tide companion deck, from the deck sheet's own notes. The deck exists to protect its Allies until two of them Bond, so the Bond is the plan and everything else is setup: `play.bond_band` prices the fused card by the bands it gains over the partners it eats, which puts fusing far ahead of the attack it is used in place of, and reads zero until both partners are on the table so the card is held rather than spent. Camp aspect 1: its constant is what protects the Allies, and advancing throws that away, so aspect and Fervor gains are both priced below zero and our own are worse than the opponent's. Get Allies out early (the Relic's search, Muster, Sudden finds). Spend the Duelist's Energy down to 0 or 1 on purpose, with the draining Arts and the self-costing Combat card, because the Allies only take control once she is spent and they all hit a band or two above her 3-to-12 ladder: `own.ally_handover` pays for the handover and `effect.energy_self` makes our own Energy a thing to spend, but only while an Ally is actually out. Win on wounds from Arts performed by Allies. The Mastery and the Arts keep the opponent's Fervor down, so their Ascension win is what we police. More blocks than the beatdown decks, and they are meant to be used. Nothing is swapped in from the Armory: the one card that starts in play does the work.
name: tide_companions
